Roman lead pig ingot c63-69AD. The ingot is rectangular in plan and trapezoid in section. Max length: 530mm tapering to 490mm; max width: 160mm tapering to 80mm; height: 110mm tapering to 90mm; weight: 63.4kg. Four clear layers can be seen giving an indication of the way in which the ingot was produced, by pouring four separate batches of metal in the mould. One end of the ingot has been lost and there are cut marks on all faces the ingot. Initial identification is thanks to Sam Moorhead, John Pearce, Roger Tomlin and Mark Lewis. The pig appears to be unique and has an inscription made up of ligatured letters which refer to one of the governors of Roman Britain, Marcus Trebellius Maximus…
